headline: Sterling has risen about half a per cent against the dollar today. Better UK growth figures and easing oil lifted it through the morning, and cooler US inflation at 16:30 Dubai added a quick jump, because it makes another Fed rise less likely.

happened.result: Core prices rose 0.2% in the month against 0.3% expected, and 3.0% on the year against 3.3%. Headline prices rose 0.3% against 0.4% expected, and 3.4% on the year against 3.7%.
happened.why: Cooler US inflation makes another Fed rate rise less likely, which lowers US yields and weakens the dollar, so each pound buys more dirhams.
happened.effect: GBP/USD jumped from 1.3285 to 1.3304 within two minutes, then eased back to about 1.3290 within half an hour.

happened.result: The ONS revised growth in April to June to 0.5% from its first estimate of 0.4%.
happened.why: A stronger UK economy makes a Bank of England rate rise more likely, which lifts the pound.
happened.effect: GBP/USD rose from 1.3247 to 1.3257 within two minutes, and sterling led the major currencies against the dollar through the European morning.

happened.result: Saudi Arabia resumed tanker loadings at its Red Sea port of Yanbu after restarting the East-West pipeline, and the US offered up to 40 million barrels from its strategic reserve. Brent was near $103 (about £77.50) a barrel.
happened.why: Cheaper oil eases US inflation worries and the demand for dollars as a safe haven, which softens the dollar.
happened.effect: US 10-year yields slipped to about 5.24%, and the dollar was mixed to softer before the US figures.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: Before today's figures, markets put about a 65% chance on another quarter-point Fed rise at the 28 October meeting. Cooler inflation weakens the case for one, and Friday's jobs report is the next test.

drivers.title: Oil and the Middle East
drivers.text: The US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz continues. Saudi Arabia's pipeline restart and the US offer of reserve oil have eased supply worries for now.

drivers.title: US bond yields
drivers.text: The US 10-year yield was about 5.24% on Wednesday morning, down slightly on the day but near its highest since 2007. High US yields keep the dollar attractive to hold.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: UK growth in April to June was revised up to 0.5%. The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 17 September, with three of the nine members voting for a rise, and Governor Bailey speaks on Thursday at 12:00 Dubai.

drivers.title: Where sterling stands
drivers.text: GBP/USD is back near 1.3290, up from a 12-week low near 1.3200 last week. The dollar index was on course for a 1.7% gain in September, its biggest monthly gain since June.

lower: US jobs figures on Friday stronger than the 90K forecast, or wages rising faster than 0.3%, which would make an October Fed rise more likely and strengthen the dollar.
Renewed escalation with Iran or in the Gulf that lifts oil again, which tends to strengthen the dollar.
A cautious tone on rates from Governor Bailey on Thursday, which would weaken the pound.
higher: US jobs figures weaker than the 90K forecast, or unemployment above 4.1%, which would make an October Fed rise less likely and weaken the dollar.
Oil easing further as Gulf supply recovers, which reduces the demand for dollars.
A firm tone on rates from Governor Bailey, which would support the pound.
watch: Friday's US jobs report at 16:30 Dubai: 90K new jobs and unemployment at 4.1% are forecast. Weaker figures would help someone selling pounds for dirhams, and stronger figures would hurt.
